A.explanation: The magnitude $2.0\text{ m}$ is correct but displacement is a vector and must include the direction from X to Y.

B.explanation: The straight line from X to Y is the diameter, $2 \times 1.0\text{ m} = 2.0\text{ m}$, directed due south.

C.explanation: About $3.1\text{ m}$ is the distance travelled along the semicircle, $\pi \times 1.0\text{ m}$, not the straight-line displacement.

D.explanation: About $3.1\text{ m}$ is the curved path length, so it cannot be the displacement even with south added.

walkthrough: Identify the start X and finish Y on the diagram. Y lies directly below X across the semicircular end of radius $1.0\text{ m}$.
State the rule: displacement is the straight-line vector from start to finish, with both magnitude and direction. Distance is the length of the path travelled.
Find the displacement magnitude as the diameter of the semicircle: $s = 2r = 2 \times 1.0\text{ m} = 2.0\text{ m}$.
Find the direction from the compass: the arrow from X to Y points toward south, so the vector is due south.
Check the distractor: the curved distance is $\pi r \approx 3.1\text{ m}$, which explains the $3.1\text{ m}$ options. This is option B.
